AI.conclusion: Real-world LLM data agents should be evaluated not merely by whether outputs match a reference answer, but by whether those outputs are backed by auditable computation. Trace Integrity and CAIT Rate provide complementary deployment-focused evaluation dimensions beyond answer accuracy.

title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic technological evolution in societies of language-model agents
summary: Collective intelligence can emerge when individuals coordinate through a shared environment, allowing local actions to accumulate into durable social organization. Language-model agents offer a new substrate for this process, yet most multi-agent systems rely on direct conversation, predefined roles, or centralized workflows. It remains unclear whether decentralized agents can build functional technologies and outperform independent search. Here, initially homogeneous LLM agents in SwarmWorld self-organize without assigned roles or recipes into evolving technological societies. Agents explore a spatial environment, process resources, test materials, construct persistent artifacts, and write executable controllers evaluated by a deterministic simulator under unseen disturbances after the agents are removed. SwarmWorld splits cognition from consequence: agents propose architectures and controllers within fixed action and material schemas, while the simulated world determines function. Shared societies develop broader, more resilient technological portfolios than a strong best-of-N isolated-search baseline, although isolated search remains competitive for the strongest artifact. Agents differentiate into exploration, construction, maintenance, and coordination behaviors, transitioning as the world matures. Technologies accumulate through collaborative construction, executable inheritance, and persistent agent-artifact networks, with most reuse beginning through physical observation rather than communication. Explicit cultural mechanisms amplify collaboration and organization, but functional benefits depend on outcome and timescale. Physical stigmergy alone supports capable societies, while interaction drives persistent technological ecologies rather than universally superior individual inventions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SwarmWorld, a testbed where initially homogeneous LLM agents self-organize into technological societies without predefined roles, communication protocols, or centralized workflows. Agents explore, construct artifacts, and write executable controllers tested by a deterministic simulator. Results show collective societies develop broader and more resilient technology portfolios than best-of-N isolated search, with agents differentiating into specialized roles and technologies accumulating via stigmergy and executable inheritance.
AI.motivation: Current multi-agent LLM systems rely on direct conversation, predefined roles, or centralized workflows, leaving open whether decentralized agents can self-organize to build functional technologies. The authors aim to test whether initially homogeneous LLM agents can form evolving technological societies through shared-environment coordination (stigmergy) and outperform independent search.
AI.method: SwarmWorld is a spatial environment where LLM agents explore, process resources, test materials, construct persistent artifacts, and write executable controllers. Cognition is separated from consequence: agents propose within fixed action/material schemas while a deterministic simulator evaluates the resulting artifacts under unseen disturbances after agents are removed. The setup includes no assigned roles or recipes, enabling measurement of emergent specialization and cultural accumulation.
AI.result: Shared societies develop broader and more resilient technological portfolios than a strong best-of-N isolated-search baseline, though isolated search remains competitive for the strongest individual artifact. Agents emerge into exploration, construction, maintenance, and coordination behaviors that transition as the world matures. Technologies accumulate through collaborative construction, executable inheritance, and persistent agent-artifact networks, with most reuse beginning through physical observation rather than communication. Explicit cultural mechanisms amplify collaboration but functional benefits depend on outcome and timescale; physical stigmergy alone supports capable societies.
AI.conclusion: Decentralized LLM agents can self-organize into functional technological societies through shared-environment coordination. Physical stigmergy alone is sufficient to support capable societies, while interaction fosters persistent technological ecologies rather than universally superior individual inventions. The separation of cognition from consequence provides a scalable and testable framework for collective intelligence in language-model agents.

title: Planetary Prediction Engine: Autonomous Geospatial Prediction via Intelligent Data Selection and Foundation Model Embeddings
summary: Addressing critical global challenges, from food security and disaster risk to disease outbreaks and socio-economic vulnerability, demands high-fidelity geospatial modeling. However, building predictive planetary models remains bottlenecked by a fragmented data ecosystem, requiring manual data retrieval, multimodal data curation and fusion along with iterative model selection. We present the Planetary Prediction Engine (PPE), an autonomous AI system that executes this end-to-end workflow directly from natural-language queries. PPE synthesizes multimodal datasets on the fly, retrieving spatiotemporally relevant covariates across open-web and Earth observation platforms (Data Commons, Google Earth Engine) and fusing them with geospatial foundation model embeddings (PDFM, AlphaEarth). Simultaneously, it searches over task-tailored model architecture families with automated overfitting guards. Across diverse tasks, geographies, and scientific domains, PPE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art or manually tuned expert baselines. For US spatial regression, PPE improves mean $R^2$ across 21 CDC health indicators (76.8% vs. 60.0%), FEMA national risk indices (64.9% vs. 60.0%), and the Social Vulnerability Index (66.2% vs. 58.6%). For spatial downscaling in data-scarce settings, PPE integrates localized proxies to double baseline accuracy in Nigerian food security indicators ($R^2$ of 66.1% vs. 31.5%). For epidemiological nowcasting of the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, PPE achieves a Recall@10 of 83.3% (identifying 15 of 18 newly invaded health zones across five weekly forecasts), a +10.3 percentage-point improvement over the public state-of-the-art modeling (~73%). By combining autonomous multimodal planetary data discovery with targeted model optimization, PPE lowers the technical barrier to planetary-scale analytics, enabling rapid, customized, expert-level deployment.

AI.tldr: PPE is an autonomous AI system that performs end-to-end planetary-scale geospatial modeling directly from natural-language queries, automatically retrieving and fusing multimodal datasets from open data platforms and geospatial foundation model embeddings, while searching over model architectures with overfitting guards. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse tasks, including US health regression (76.8% R² vs 60.0%), food security downscaling in Nigeria (66.1% vs 31.5%), and Ebola outbreak nowcasting in DRC (Recall@10 of 83.3%).
AI.motivation: Building predictive planetary models is bottlenecked by a fragmented data ecosystem requiring manual data retrieval, multimodal curation/fusion, and iterative model selection. This high technical barrier prevents rapid, expert-level deployment of geospatial analytics to address critical global challenges.
AI.method: PPE executes an autonomous end-to-end workflow from natural-language queries: (1) synthesizes multimodal datasets on the fly by retrieving spatiotemporally relevant covariates across open-web and Earth observation platforms (Data Commons, Google Earth Engine); (2) fuses retrieved data with geospatial foundation model embeddings (PDFM, AlphaEarth); (3) searches over task-tailored model architecture families with automated overfitting guards.
AI.result: Across diverse tasks and geographies, PPE outperforms SOTA baselines: US spatial regression improves mean R² across 21 CDC health indicators (76.8% vs 60.0%), FEMA national risk indices (64.9% vs 60.0%), and Social Vulnerability Index (66.2% vs 58.6%). In data-scarce Nigerian food security downscaling, it doubles baseline accuracy (66.1% vs 31.5%). For epidemiological nowcasting of the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, it achieves Recall@10 of 83.3% (15/18 newly invaded health zones), a +10.3 percentage-point improvement over public SOTA (~73%).
AI.conclusion: By combining autonomous multimodal planetary data discovery with targeted model optimization, PPE lowers the technical barrier to planetary-scale analytics, enabling rapid, customized, expert-level deployment across scientific domains and geographies.
